title: Atlas Retail — Before/After Redwood Optimize Savings Scan
content:
Executive summary:

This note captures a targeted before/after savings simulation for Atlas Retail (ecommerce recommendation pipeline) based on Redwood Optimize recommendations. The goal: quantify token-level and infra-level savings over a 6‑month ramp if Atlas adopts our recommended config changes. This is a working draft for the Atlas GTM and Solutions teams; numbers are simulation-based and will be validated against Atlas telemetry during the proof-of-concept.

Key takeaways:
- Baseline monthly inference spend (hosted + dedicated bursts): $182k
- One-time integration & rollout estimate: $18k (engineering + validation)
- After Redwood Optimize recommendations (quantization + batching + routing + cache): projected monthly spend: $96k -> ~47% ongoing savings
- Peak tail-latency impact: median latency steady, P95 increases by ~20% in worst-case (mitigated by canary and fallback policies)
- Estimated 3–4 week rollout to production with canary and automatic fallback

Customer profile (Atlas Retail):
- Use case: real‑time product recommendations + similarity search for cart-saves and in-session personalization
- Traffic pattern: 07:00–23:00 daily peak, weekly spikes during promotions (~2.7x normal)
- Average request size: 256 tokens input + 64 tokens output for explainability strings
- Current model: open-llm-retail-13B (FP16), hosted primary with Dedicated reserved capacity for peak windows
- Monthly active inference requests: ~12.5M; average tokens/month: ~1.4B

Methodology / simulation assumptions:
- Baseline uses Atlas-provided billing export (Nov–Dec 2024) and telemetry sample (token distribution, sequence lengths, real latencies).
- We simulate a 6M token sample and replay through the Redwood runtime pricing/timing model to estimate per-token GPU seconds and cost.
- Hardware mix assumed: g5x2 (60%), g5x1 (30%), dedicated instances for scheduled peaks (10%) — matches Atlas reported allocation
- Baseline model config: open-llm-retail-13B, FP16, no prefix caching, concurrency=4 per GPU slot, batching disabled most of the time due to low request coalescing on Atlas SDK
- Pricing: Redwood hosted rate assumptions for simulation: $0.000022 / input token, $0.000030 / output token (hosted blended), Dedicated hourly amortized costs using Atlas committed SLO bucket included

Baseline cost breakdown (monthly) — derived from telemetry sample:
- Token processing (hosted): $138,000
- Dedicated reserved capacity (peak hours amortized): $28,500
- Request overhead (network & small infra charges): $15,500
- Total baseline: $182,000

Observed inefficiencies (evidence):
1) No KV prefix cache for repeated session prefixes — ~18% of requests share top-10 tokens, large avoidable generation cost.
2) FP16 execution without quantization — quantization could reduce GPU memory and improve packing, especially for 13B.
3) Low batching due to client SDK concurrency settings; payloads are often micro-batched with identical sequence lengths but not queued.
4) Model over-provisioning during non-peak hours — dedicated capacity is not autoscaled aggressively, causing amortized waste.

Redwood Optimize recommendations (concise):
A) Prefix/KV caching for sessioned recommendations (TTL=15m, LRU): expected to reduce repeated token cost by 65% on cached requests.
B) 8-bit quantization (Q4 or RTN path recommended for this model) with validation set: target 95% pass on fidelity checks.
C) Dynamic batching at runtime with sequence-length aware bucketting; target effective batch sizes 16–32 during peak.
D) Model routing to smaller variant for low-complexity requests (open-llm-retail-6B for 40% of lookup traffic).
E) Autoscaling policy refactor for Dedicated: scale-to-zero for non-peak + scheduled reserved buffers for promotions.
F) Instrumentation: add per-route quality evals and token-level cost attribution in Console for 90-day monitoring.

Projected after-optimization monthly cost (simulation):
- Token processing (after quant + cache + batching + model routing): $58,400
- Dedicated reserved capacity (reduced by autoscaling & routing): $23,000
- Request overhead & monitoring uplift: $14,600
- Total post-Optimize: $96,000
- Gross savings: $86,000 monthly (~47% reduction)
- One-time rollout/engineering: $18,000 (includes validation compute, canary traffic shaping, small data migration for cache keys).

Breakdown of savings contributors (approx):
- Quantization: 28% of savings (largely from lower GPU seconds and better packing)
- Prefix caching: 22% of savings (higher on repeat sessions)
- Batching: 18% of savings (peak efficiency improvements)
- Model routing (6B for trivial lookups): 16%
- Autoscale & scheduling: 8%

Sensitivity analysis (key knobs):
- Fidelity slippage: if quantization validation pass rate target drops to 80% (requiring fallbacks), effective savings drop to ~32% (some requests will fallback to FP16).
- Cache hit rate: baseline 25% assumed; if hit falls to 12% due to TTL mismatch, projected savings reduce by ~9 points.
- Promotion spikes: if promotions exceed 4x normal, Dedicated buffer must increase, temporarily reducing savings by ~6–9% during those windows.

Rollout plan (3–4 weeks):
Week 0–1: Integration + unit tests
- Implement prefix cache in the Atlas SDK (client-side keys) and server-side TTL policies.
- Add metric hooks for cache hits, per-route token cost, and model selection counts.

Week 1–2: Canary + quantization validation
- Run 10% traffic through quantized model variant and compare outputs using Atlas eval set (PSNR / similarity threshold rules).
- If fidelity within limits, increase to 40% and monitor quality signals.

Week 2–3: Full rollout of batching + routing policies
- Enable dynamic batching on serving runtime, tune sequence buckets.
- Route low-complexity requests to 6B. Observe P95 latency and error rate.

Week 3–4: Dedicated autoscale schedule and monitoring
- Update Dedicated autoscaler; add scheduled promotion buffer and fallbacks to hosted if insufficient capacity.
- Run two promotion day dry runs.

Risks & mitigations:
- Quality regression from quantization: mitigation -> conservative rollout + automatic fallback to FP16 + A/B checks on business metrics (CTR, conversions).
- Cache key collisions or staleness: mitigation -> namespaced keys (customer_id:session_id:prefix_hash) and short TTL for personalization-sensitive content.
- Latency increases at P95: mitigation -> hybrid routing with lower-latency instance pool and throttled batching for tail requests.

Open questions for Atlas:
- What is the acceptable fidelity threshold for quantized outputs on recommendation ranking? (Product asks for minimal impact to top-5 recall)
- Can Atlas modify SDK concurrency defaults for client-side coalescing? (small change on web signal gating could materially improve batching)
- Promotion forecasting API: can Atlas provide calendar of promo windows for the next 6 months to tune scheduled buffers?

Appendix A — example per-route simulation snippet (summary):
- Route: cart-recommender-v2
- Request mix: 45% lookup (short, 64 tokens), 35% blended recommend (256 tokens), 20% explainability (300–600 tokens)
- Baseline cost per 1M tokens: $22.8k (end-to-end blended)
- Post-optimize cost per 1M tokens: $12.0k

Appendix B — validation checklist (deliverable during POC):
- Regression tests (top-k recall, CTR surrogate) pass at 95% threshold
- Cost telemetry accurately attributed per-route in Console
- Canary rollback working and tested for traffic cutover

Next steps / asks:
- Internal: Solutions Eng (Elliot) to schedule 2‑hour scoping call with Atlas infra + data teams next week.
- Atlas: provide sample billing export and 7‑day telemetry stream (token-level) for run-through validation.
- Product: finalize conservative quantization policy and default TTLs for prefix cache.

Notes on data privacy: all telemetry used in the simulation was provided under Atlas NDA. Cache architecture recommended aligns with Atlas data-retention policies and does not persist PII.

Document status: working draft. Intended to be updated after POC telemetry is completed (JIRA-OPT-1293).
